clue.text: Non-RP sound upset Nigel's mum

parts.note: a sound is an inlet or arm of the sea, as an estuary is

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the name and the silencing word are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the name Nigel; the possessive adds no letter
to keep mum is to say nothing, as the hushing word sh demands

explanation.surface: Someone with a non-standard accent mispronounces things and annoys Nigel's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: RP is Received Pronunciation, the traditional prestige accent of southern England. 'upset' rearranges NIGEL plus SH (mum, as in 'keep mum').
explanation.definitionFit: Estuary English is the London-and-Thames accent that departs from Received Pronunciation, so it is a non-RP way of speaking.

clue.text: Initial advantage to English at the side of Nelson maybe

parts.note: a nelson is a wrestling hold, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: England's early advantage came from being beside Admiral Nelson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nelson' suggests the admiral but is the wrestling grip with the arms under the opponent's.
explanation.definitionFit: A toehold is a small first footing from which to progress, an initial advantage.

clue.text: Greedy fool returns after end of tea

indicators.note: after says the reversed fool follows that letter
end of picks out the closing letter of tea
returns means the word for a fool comes back the other way

parts.note: div is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A greedy idiot comes back once tea is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or keen to the point of craving, as greedy is.

clue.text: Amenable Scottish individual embodying the opposite of casual at golf

indicators.note: embodying means containing, so the Scots word wraps the turned word

parts.note: yin is Scots for one, an individual

indicators.note: the opposite of here means the word for casual is taken the opposite way round

parts.note: idle means casual, unoccupied
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An easy-going Scot is anything but casual on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: Yin is a Scots word for one. 'golf' supplies the NATO-alphabet letter, not the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding means compliant and giving way easily, which is what amenable describes.

clue.text: Idiot can back ingenuity

indicators.note: back means the word for a can is read in reverse

parts.note: a tin is a can
wit is cleverness or ingenuity

explanation.surface: An idiot is able to support cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a foolish person, an idiot.

clue.text: So far lethargy is uncommon

indicators.note: uncommon means out of the ordinary, so the letters of the two words take an unusual order

explanation.surface: Up to now, lethargy is rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So far' reads as 'until now' but means a great distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-years are vast distances, used figuratively for things very far apart, so far as an adverb.

clue.text: Girl in Sweden new in steamy sauna

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

indicators.note: steamy suggests things heated and churned up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A girl in Sweden is new to the hot sauna.
explanation.definitionFit: Susanna is a girl's given name.

clue.text: See red and end up like a disgraced tabloid editor?

definitions.meaning: to see red is to become very angry

definitions.text: end up like a disgraced tabloid editor?
definitions.meaning: a rag is a downmarket newspaper, so a sacked editor is parted from the paper

explanation.surface: A disgraced tabloid editor loses their temper as their career ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose one's rag' is British slang for losing one's temper; a rag is also a tabloid paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's rag is a British idiom for flying into a rage, which is seeing red.

clue.text: What's left for O'Connor comeback? It's entertaining troops

indicators.note: a comeback turns the singer's first name round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Des O'Connor was a British TV entertainer and singer

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as guests, so the word for it wraps around the soldiers

parts.note: the word it; the 's is a link
troops are soldiers, men

explanation.surface: A comeback show for Des O'Connor is wondered about as it entertains the soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Des O'Connor was a long-running British TV host and singer; 'for O'Connor' is just his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is the matter that settles and remains at the bottom, so it is what is left behind.

clue.text: Delight in tips from gardeners ushering slugs to oblivion

indicators.note: the tips of the five words that follow are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Gardeners take pleasure in dispatching slugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment or relish, the same as delight taken in doing something.

clue.text: Part of academic year consisting of science and language

parts.note: a term is one division of the school or university year
in can mean consisting of, as in a set in three parts
an ology is a jocular word for any science

explanation.surface: A course spanning one term combines science with a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ology' was made famous in an old British Telecom advert where a grandson's 'ology' was celebrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminology is the specialised vocabulary of a field, its language.

clue.text: Could bedrooms off and on be his playground?

definitions.text: Could bedrooms off and on be his playground?

indicators.note: off and on means intermittently, so only every other letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: Bedrooms as the playground of the god of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off and on' keeps the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of bedrooms; the whole clue then describes the love god, whose playground a bedroom might well be.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of sexual love, for whom bedrooms would be a natural playground.

clue.text: Letting in a ball stopped by hand

indicators.note: stopped by means plugged in the middle, so the word for a hand goes into the dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper concedes a goal when a ball is stopped with the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads: 'ball' is a formal dance, and 'hand' is a slang word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittance is the act of allowing entry, a noun matching the gerund letting in.

clue.text: Sheltered from reality, minor celeb admits nothing in confrontation with journalist

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the minor celebrity's word takes in the zero

parts.note: a C-lister is a minor celebrity
O is zero, nothing
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A sheltered minor celebrity admits to nothing when confronted by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confrontation with' just sets the journalist beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloistered means secluded as in a monastery, so shut away from the real world.

clue.text: Confusing Independent for Unionist moderate

indicators.note: Independent for Unionist means one abbreviation takes the other's place

parts.note: confusing means muddling

explanation.surface: A political commentator mixes up Independents and Unionists, which a moderate would find muddling.
explanation.walkthrough: In UK politics Independent and Unionist are both party labels, abbreviated I and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling means of medium or fair quality, neither good nor bad, which is moderate.

clue.text: Alight having missed right stop

indicators.note: having missed says one letter is left out of the getting-off word

parts.note: to alight from a train is to detrain

explanation.surface: A passenger gets off having missed the correct station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alight' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to get off a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain someone is to stop or hold them back, a verb matching stop.

clue.text: Dead newt by Scottish water facility

parts.note: an eft is a newt
Loch Ness is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A dead newt found beside a Scottish waterworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facility' looks like a building but means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility as skill or ease of performance is deftness, the quality of being nimble.

clue.text: New global organisation getting firm about international ambassador

parts.note: UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the firm's abbreviation goes round the letter for international

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A new world body hires a company to deal with an international envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal ambassador, the Pope's diplomatic representative to a foreign state.

clue.text: Sort of thing that is rarely seen by day?

definitions.text: Sort of thing that is rarely seen by day?

indicators.note: sort means to arrange, so the letters of the word are put in another order

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A kind of thing seldom seen in daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: nightwear is rarely on view in daytime.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, worn in bed and so seldom seen in daytime.

clue.text: Energy put into much smaller game

indicators.note: put into means the symbol for energy is placed inside the phrase

parts.note: much smaller is far less
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energy is invested in a far smaller project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is the adjective, as in game for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Game as an adjective means brave and willing, and fearless means without fear, so both describe the bold.

clue.text: Model designed with nothing in timber

indicators.note: in says the two letters go inside the reworked word
designed means fashioned to a plan, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A model is designed with nothing in the way of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' turns MODEL into ELMOD, and 'in' puts W and O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmwood is the wood of the elm tree, used as timber.

clue.text: Claim palaeolithic fragment could be creature

indicators.note: fragment says a piece of the phrase is broken off to give the word

explanation.surface: A palaeontologist claims a bone fragment may be from some animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An impala is an African antelope, so it is a creature.

clue.text: Justifiable to run away with his second partner?

parts.note: to leg it is slang for running away

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the word his

parts.note: a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Is it justifiable to elope with one's second wife?
explanation.walkthrough: 'his second' looks like 'his second partner' but is the second letter of his. 'Leg it' is British slang for running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means valid or defensible, which is what justifiable means.

clue.text: Prog rock initially banned from broadcast; turn over for a classic

indicators.note: turn over says what remains is flipped and read from the end back
banned from says the named letters are thrown out of the broadcast

parts.note: a broadcast is a programme

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of rock

explanation.surface: Prog rock is banned from the airwaves, so switch over to a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: PROG and R (rock initially) come off PROGRAMME to leave AMME; 'turn over' makes it EMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's novel, a classic of English literature.

clue.text: Less men suffering memory loss may be continent

indicators.note: less means minus, so letters come out of the memory loss word

parts.note: amnesia is memory loss
men suffering means the letters of men in a disturbed order, as they sit in the word for memory loss

explanation.surface: Fewer men suffering memory loss may be restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continent' looks like an adjective (self-restrained) but is the landmass; M, N, E from 'suffering' men come out of AMNESIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the world's continents.

clue.text: Predator almost devoured drenched in endless blood

indicators.note: drenched in means steeped inside, so the shortened eating word sits within the shortened blood word
endless says the last letter of the blood word goes

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

indicators.note: almost says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: devoured means ate

explanation.surface: A predator nearly ate something soaked in blood.
explanation.walkthrough: Both shortenings drop a final E before one goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A gator, short for alligator, is a large reptilian hunter, a predator.

clue.text: Dislike American translation

parts.note: a version is a translation, as of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes the American rendering of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike, a noun matching dislike.

clue.text: Safeguard inactive board member's name

parts.note: inactive means lifeless, dead
a chess piece is a man on the board; the possessive keeps its s
a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A dormant company director's name serves as a safety measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board member' suggests a company director but means a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead man's handle is a control that stops a train if the driver lets go, a safety device.
